lines.text: If a nuclear bomb goes off near you, you have about ten minutes to save your life. Here's exactly what to do.

phrases.text: If a nuclear bomb goes off near you,
you have about ten minutes to save your life.
Here's exactly what to do.

lines.text: First, the flash. Don't look: it can blind you. Drop face down and cover your head.

phrases.text: First, the flash.
Don't look: it can blind you.
Drop face down and cover your head.

lines.text: Seconds later, the blast wave hits. Stay down until it passes. Then stay away from windows: flying glass kills.

phrases.text: Seconds later, the blast wave hits.
Stay down until it passes.
Then stay away from windows: flying glass kills.

lines.text: Then get inside. Brick or concrete, in the basement or the middle of the building. Not your car: it barely protects you.

phrases.text: Then get inside.
Brick or concrete, in the basement or the middle of the building.
Not your car: it barely protects you.

lines.text: Because the fallout is coming: radioactive dust, deadliest in the first hours.

phrases.text: Because the fallout is coming:
radioactive dust, deadliest in the first hours.

lines.text: After seven hours, it's ten times weaker. After two days, a hundred times.

phrases.text: After seven hours, it's ten times weaker.
After two days, a hundred times.

lines.text: So stay inside for at least twenty-four hours. Don't go looking for family: they should shelter where they are.

phrases.text: So stay inside for at least twenty-four hours.
Don't go looking for family: they should shelter where they are.

lines.text: Would you know where to go? Tell me in the comments.

phrases.text: Would you know where to go?
Tell me in the comments.
